facts.statement: Yingshanosaurus is an extinct genus of stegosaurian dinosaurs found in what is now Southwestern China.
facts.quote: Yingshanosaurus (meaning "Yingshan lizard") is an extinct genus of stegosaurian dinosaurs from the Middle Jurassic of what is now Southwestern China.

facts.statement: A partial skeleton of Yingshanosaurus was discovered in 1983.
facts.quote: It is known from a partial skeleton discovered in 1983

facts.statement: The only known species, Yingshanosaurus jichuanensis, was named and described in 1994.
facts.quote: The genus contains a single species, Yingshanosaurus jichuanensis, named and described in 1994.

facts.statement: A villager in Jichuan, Sichuan Province, China, discovered the skeleton while digging a house foundation in 1983.
facts.quote: In 1983, a villager in the town of Jichuan discovered a partial associated dinosaur skeleton while digging the foundation for his house in Yingshan County of Sichuan Province, China.

facts.statement: Zhu Songlin formally described the genus and species in 1994, designating the skeleton as holotype specimen CV00722.
facts.quote: In 1994, Zhu Songlin described Yingshanosaurus jichuanensis as a distinct genus and species of stegosaurian dinosaurs, establishing the partial skeleton as the holotype specimen, CV00722.

facts.statement: Between 1992 and 1993, the specimen was displayed in Japan under the mistranslated name "Yunshanosaurus".
facts.quote: Through 1992 and 1993, a mounted skeleton of this specimen was displayed in a Japanese exhibition of Chinese dinosaurs, where it was also referenced under the mistranslated title "Yunshanosaurus".

facts.statement: Many researchers outside China were unaware of Yingshanosaurus for years due to the limited availability of the 1994 description.
facts.quote: Due to the limited availability of Zhu's 1994 publication, the validity of Yingshanosaurus went unnoticed by many researchers outside of China

facts.statement: Yingshanosaurus was a slow-moving, quadrupedal herbivore.
facts.quote: Like other stegosaurs, Yingshanosaurus was a slow-moving, quadrupedal herbivore.

facts.statement: Yingshanosaurus was a medium-sized dinosaur, measuring 4 to 5 meters in length.
facts.quote: At 4 - 5 m long, it is a medium-sized member of this group.

facts.statement: Yingshanosaurus had flattened, semi-triangular plates arranged in pairs along its neck, back, and tail.
facts.quote: Several flattened, semi-triangular plates were arranged in pairs along the neck, back, and tail.

facts.statement: A large spine near the shoulder likely served to protect the torso from predators.
facts.quote: The large spine near its shoulder likely functioned as a form of protection from predators for its torso.

facts.statement: Unlike many earlier stegosaurs, the holes between the vertebrae in the sacrum of Yingshanosaurus were almost completely closed.
facts.quote: Unlike many earlier species, the fenestrae (holes) between vertebrae in the sacrum are almost completely closed.

facts.statement: Its anatomy suggests Yingshanosaurus belonged to the more exclusive subfamily Stegosaurinae.
facts.quote: its anatomy suggests it had derived traits consistent with members of the more exclusive subfamily Stegosaurinae.

facts.statement: Fossils of Yingshanosaurus come from the Upper Shaximiao Formation, dating to the Bathonian age of the Jurassic.
facts.quote: Yingshanosaurus is known from the Upper Shaximiao Formation, which dates to the Bathonian age of the Jurassic period.

facts.statement: The exact purpose of Yingshanosaurus's osteoderms is a subject of debate among scientists.
facts.quote: The purpose of these osteoderms is debated.

facts.statement: Researchers suggest the plates may have been used for display, species recognition, or thermoregulation.
facts.quote: The plates have been suggested to play a role in display, species recognition, or thermoregulation.

facts.statement: The spikes at the tail tip, known as a 'thagomizer', likely served as defensive structures.
facts.quote: In contrast, the spikes at the end of the tail, sometimes referred to as the 'thagomizer', likely served as defensive structures.

facts.statement: Typical traits of its clade include a small head, short forelimbs, long hindlimbs, and short hand and foot bones.
facts.quote: Other traits typical of species in this clade include a proportionally small head, short forelimbs, longer column-like hindlimbs, and short metacarpals and metatarsals.

facts.statement: Bone fusion in the holotype indicates that the individual was a mature adult.
facts.quote: Based on the fusion of several bones, including the scapula to the coracoid and the tibia to the fibula, the Yingshanosaurus holotype can be identified as a mature adult individual.

facts.statement: Some researchers argue the name should be considered invalid because the original description was difficult to find.
facts.quote: In their 2006 review of Chinese stegosaurs, Maidment & Wei stated they were unable to find a description, a diagnosis, or any published figures of the Yingshanosaurus fossils, and, as such, the name should be recognized as a nomen nudum.

facts.statement: Although the validity of the name has been reaffirmed, it is rarely cited in international scientific literature.
facts.quote: While the validity of Yingshanosaurus has subsequently been reaffirmed, it is rarely mentioned in the scientific literature outside of China.

facts.statement: Nine dorsal vertebrae have been identified for Yingshanosaurus.
facts.quote: In total, nine dorsal vertebrae are known for Yingshanosaurus.

facts.statement: The sacrum of Yingshanosaurus consists of five vertebrae that are firmly fused together.
facts.quote: The sacrum is composed of five firmly fused vertebrae, the first of which is a dorsosacral (reinforced dorsal vertebra).

facts.statement: Seven fairly complete tail vertebrae are known for Yingshanosaurus.
facts.quote: Seven fairly complete caudal vertebrae are known for Yingshanosaurus.

facts.statement: The humerus of Yingshanosaurus measures 40 cm in length.
facts.quote: The humerus is 40 cm long, with a short shaft.

facts.statement: The radius of Yingshanosaurus is 30.5 cm long.
facts.quote: The radius, a simple straight bone expanded on both ends, is 30.5 cm long.

facts.statement: The ilia of Yingshanosaurus have a maximum preserved length of 80 cm.
facts.quote: Both ilia are preserved, with a maximum length of 80 cm.

facts.statement: The femur of Yingshanosaurus is 67.5 cm long.
facts.quote: The femur is 67.5 cm long, with a straight shaft and well-developed greater trochanter.

facts.statement: The fused tibia and fibula of Yingshanosaurus reach a maximum length of about 46 cm.
facts.quote: The tibia and fibula are firmly fused to each other, with a maximum length of about 46 cm.

facts.statement: The holotype of Yingshanosaurus includes five nearly complete osteoderms from various body regions.
facts.quote: The Yingshanosaurus holotype includes five nearly complete osteoderms—large bony structures embedded in the skin—from various regions of the body.

facts.statement: The largest osteoderm of Yingshanosaurus is an 80 cm long parascapular spine from the shoulder.
facts.quote: The largest of these, at about 80 cm long, is a left parascapular spine from the shoulder region.

facts.statement: The large shoulder spine of Yingshanosaurus likely functioned as trunk protection and may have rotated slightly around the scapula.
facts.quote: This spine almost certainly functioned as a protection for the trunk, and may have been able to rotate slightly around the scapula.

facts.statement: Yingshanosaurus had dorsal plates arranged in symmetrical pairs, unlike the staggered rows seen in Stegosaurus.
facts.quote: The plates of Yingshanosaurus were arranged in symmetrical pairs along the dorsal midline, contrasting with some stegosaurs like Stegosaurus, where the plates were in a staggered, alternating row.

facts.statement: Zhu noted that the femur-to-tibia ratio of Yingshanosaurus is more similar to Kentrosaurus than to Stegosaurus or Dacentrurus.
facts.quote: He also observed that the ratio of the femur to tibia length is more similar to the stegosaurid Kentrosaurus, than to Stegosaurus and Dacentrurus.

facts.statement: Early reconstructions incorrectly placed Yingshanosaurus's large shoulder spines near the pelvic girdle as 'parasacral spines' before Gigantspinosaurus clarified their position.
facts.quote: Before the discovery of the Gigantspinosaurus holotype, which preserves both parascapular spines in articulation with the rest of the body, the identity of these large osteoderms and their articulation with the body was unclear, and some early reconstructions placed them near the pelvic girdle as "parasacral spines".

facts.statement: The transverse processes of Yingshanosaurus project at an angle of about 60 degrees relative to the neural spine.
facts.quote: The transverse processes project at angle of about 60° relative to the neural spine.

facts.statement: Yingshanosaurus possessed seven haemal arches with typical stegosaur anatomy, differing from the inverted T-shape of Kentrosaurus.
facts.quote: Seven haemal arches were found which demonstrate typical stegosaur anatomy, contrasting with the inverted T-shape seen in the haemal arches of Kentrosaurus.

facts.statement: Early estimates in 2011 placed the age of Yingshanosaurus fossils in the Middle Jurassic, specifically the Bajocian to Bathonian stages.
facts.quote: estimates in 2011 proposed a Bajocian–Bathonian age range in the Middle Jurassic epoch.

facts.statement: Later research established the Bathonian stage as the oldest possible age for the Upper Member of the Shaximiao Formation where Yingshanosaurus was found.
facts.quote: subsequent research determined that the older Lower Member could be reliably dated to the Bathonian, setting this as the oldest possible age for the Upper Member.

facts.statement: Yingshanosaurus lived during the Late Jurassic, approximately 155 million years ago in the Kimmeridgian stage.
facts.quote: que vivió a finales del período Jurásico, hace aproximadamente 155 millones de años, en el Kimmeridgiense

facts.statement: Yingshanosaurus measured between four and five meters in length.
facts.quote: Medía entre cuatro a cinco metros de largo.

facts.statement: Unlike some other stegosaurs, the dorsal plates of Yingshanosaurus lacked a thickened middle section and were uniformly flattened with a venous and rough surface.
facts.quote: Estas no tenían "ensanches", es decir, una sección más gruesa en el medio, sino que eran uniformemente aplanadas, con una superficie venosa y rugosa.

facts.statement: A stegosaur skeleton was excavated in Sichuan in 1983 by a team led by Wan Jihou.
facts.quote: En 1983, un esqueleto de estegosaurio fue excavado en Sichuan por un equipo liderado por Wan Jihou.

facts.statement: The discovery was reported by Zhou Shiwu in 1984.
facts.quote: En 1984, el hallazgo fue reportado por Zhou Shiwu.

facts.statement: Zhu Songlin provided a complete description of the animal in 1994.
facts.quote: En 1994 Zhu Songlin realizó una descripción completa del animal.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen CV OO722 was found in a late layer of the Upper Shaximiao Formation, likely dating to the early Kimmeridgian.
facts.quote: El holotipo, CV OO722, fue hallado en una capa tardía de la Formación Shaximiao Superior, que probablemente data de inicios del Kimmeridgiense.

facts.statement: A 2006 study by Susannah Maidment concluded that the only known fossil specimen of Yingshanosaurus could not be located.

facts.statement: The Paleobiology Database lists the parent group of Yingshanosaurus as Stegosauridae.

facts.statement: The Paleobiology Database records the time range of Yingshanosaurus as the Bathonian to Callovian stages, between 168.2 and 161.5 million years ago.

facts.statement: Like all stegosaurs, Yingshanosaurus was a herbivorous dinosaur.

facts.statement: Yingshanosaurus had medium-height neural arches, and the neural spines of its dorsal vertebrae were plate-shaped with a transversely expanded top.

facts.statement: The genus name Yingshanosaurus is derived from the locality of Yingshan, while the species name refers to the location of the locality, Jichuan.
facts.quote: El nombre del género se deriva de la localidad de Yingshan. El nombre de la especie se refiere a la ubicación de la localidad, Jichuan.
